method: Manual native Chrome interaction through accessibility controls and screenshots; no browser JavaScript injection.

checks.result: Both Ontario source cards connected; extra panel showed current prices for both books, alternate spreads and best-identical-line labels.
Market selector exposed alternate spreads, alternate totals, touchdowns, passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and receptions.
Passing-yards selection showed inclusive N+ labels, separate-contract wording, DraftKings early-exit protection and FanDuel Bet Protect. Searching Jordan filtered to Jordan Love.

checks.surface: Chrome responsive preview, 375 x 800 CSS pixels
checks.result: Main board and preference controls fit the narrow viewport; toolbar wrapped and main price cells remained readable. This was a visual board-layout check, not a full mobile interaction suite.
Favorites filter, saved dark/compact preferences, comparison grid, available-history chart and keyboard-help dialog were exercised.
D and C toggled dark and compact controls; selecting Comparison grid rendered separate book columns and same-line comparison headings.
Market estimates opened with same-line margin, fair-chance and EV values, plus explicit assumptions about settled win/loss, exclusions, and non-guaranteed arbitrage candidates.

limits: These are the controls and layouts directly observed; the report does not claim every browser, device or interaction was tested.
The 375-pixel check predates b14c22f; the stylesheet did not change between those releases. Later UI changes covered labels, ranking guards and scroll/focus preservation.
Persistent history is verified independently by the cloud restart report, rather than inferred from a chart screenshot.
These checks do not measure bookmaker-to-screen or visible price-change latency.
